```{python}
#| echo: false
# Every number on this page is computed by mlsysim when the site builds.
# Nothing here is typed by hand, so the page cannot drift from the engine.
import sys
from pathlib import Path

for candidate in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]:
    pkg_dir = candidate / "mlsysim"
    if (pkg_dir / "mlsysim" / "__init__.py").exists():
        if str(pkg_dir) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(pkg_dir))
        break

import mlsysim
from mlsysim import Engine, Hardware, Models
from mlsysim.solvers import ServingModel

VERSION = mlsysim.__version__

# Single-node roofline: ResNet-50 at batch 1 on an A100.
resnet = Engine.solve(
    model=Models.Vision.ResNet50, hardware=Hardware.Cloud.A100,
    batch_size=1, precision="fp16",
)
r_lat = resnet.latency.to("ms").magnitude
r_tput = resnet.throughput.to("1/s").magnitude
r_compute = resnet.latency_compute.to("ms").magnitude
r_memory = resnet.latency_memory.to("ms").magnitude
r_overhead = resnet.latency_overhead.to("ms").magnitude
r_ai = resnet.arithmetic_intensity.magnitude
a100 = Hardware.Cloud.A100
ridge = (a100.compute.peak_flops / a100.memory.bandwidth).to("flop/byte").magnitude

# LLM serving: Llama 3 8B on an H100 with a 2,048-token prompt.
SEQ = 2048
llama = ServingModel().solve(
    model=Models.Language.Llama3_8B, hardware=Hardware.Cloud.H100, seq_len=SEQ,
)
ttft = llama.ttft.to("ms").magnitude
itl = llama.itl.to("ms").magnitude
# GiB throughout: the H100's capacity is specified as 80 GiB.
weights_gib = llama.model_weights_size.to("GiB").magnitude
kv_gib = llama.kv_cache_size.to("GiB").magnitude
h100_gib = Hardware.Cloud.H100.memory.capacity.to("GiB").magnitude

# Registry sizes, counted from the live registries.
def count(registry):
    seen, stack = set(), [registry]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        for name in dir(node):
            if name.startswith("_"):
                continue
            item = getattr(node, name)
            if isinstance(item, type):
                stack.append(item)
            elif hasattr(item, "name") and hasattr(item, "metadata"):
                seen.add(id(item))
    return len(seen)

n_hardware = count(Hardware)
n_models = count(Models)
n_physics = sum(1 for n in mlsysim.physics.__all__ if n.startswith("calc_"))
n_solvers = sum(1 for n in mlsysim.solvers.__all__ if not n.startswith("Base"))
```

MLSys·im is an analytical modeling framework for the stage before you benchmark or provision hardware. It makes first-order constraints explicit (memory, compute, network, data, reliability, cost, and carbon) so you can narrow the design space and decide which experiments are worth running.

## Start with the system question

Each question below maps to a solver. Ask it analytically first, then validate the sensitive parameters on the real stack once hardware is available.

::: {.sim-grid .sim-grid-2}

::: {.sim-card}
**Will it fit?**

Estimate weights, activations, optimizer state, KV cache, and communication buffers before a job fails at runtime.
:::

::: {.sim-card}
**What binds?**

Separate compute, memory bandwidth, network communication, data input, reliability, cost, and carbon constraints.
:::

::: {.sim-card}
**How much capacity?**

Size serving replicas for a QPS and p99 target, including batching and queueing assumptions.
:::

::: {.sim-card}
**What should I tune?**

Sweep batch size, precision, parallelism, efficiency, geography, and hardware without needing cluster access.
:::

:::

## Try it in five lines

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
from mlsysim import Engine, Models, Hardware

profile = Engine.solve(
    model=Models.Vision.ResNet50,
    hardware=Hardware.Cloud.A100,
    batch_size=1,
    precision="fp16",
)

print(f"Bottleneck: {profile.bottleneck}")
print(f"Latency:    {profile.latency.to('ms'):~.2f}")
print(f"Throughput: {profile.throughput.to('1/s'):~.0f}")
```

The engine applies the roofline model [@williams2009]: a step takes at least as long as its compute time or its memory-transfer time, whichever is larger.

$$T = \max\!\left(\frac{\text{FLOPs}}{\text{Peak} \times \eta},\ \frac{\text{Bytes}}{\text{BW}}\right) + T_{\text{overhead}}$$

At batch 1, ResNet-50's arithmetic intensity is `{python} f"{r_ai:.0f}"` FLOP/byte, just under the A100's ridge point of `{python} f"{ridge:.0f}"` FLOP/byte. The compute term (`{python} f"{r_compute:.3f}"` ms) edges out the memory term (`{python} f"{r_memory:.3f}"` ms), but both are small next to the fixed dispatch overhead of `{python} f"{r_overhead:.3f}"` ms. The `{python} f"{r_lat:.2f}"` ms total is mostly overhead, which is why batching helps so much here. Start from the [Model Zoo](zoo/models.qmd) and [Silicon Zoo](zoo/hardware.qmd), or define your own workload and hardware.

## What you can model

Every solver takes typed registry objects and returns an analytical estimate with units attached.

::: {.sim-grid .sim-grid-3}

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Roofline analysis**

Compute versus memory bottlenecks, single-node latency and throughput.

[Hello Roofline →](tutorials/00_hello_roofline.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**LLM serving**

Time to first token, inter-token latency, and KV-cache pressure. Llama 3 8B on an H100 with a `{python} f"{SEQ:,}"`-token prompt: `{python} f"{ttft:.0f}"` ms to first token, `{python} f"{itl:.1f}"` ms per token after that.

[Two Phases of Inference →](tutorials/02_two_phases.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Memory and capacity**

Training memory breakdowns, serving replicas, and MoE routing imbalance. The same Llama 3 8B needs `{python} f"{weights_gib:.0f}"` GiB of weights plus `{python} f"{kv_gib:.2f}"` GiB of KV cache, out of `{python} f"{h100_gib:.0f}"` GiB on the H100.

[Memory, Capacity, and MoE →](tutorials/11_training_memory_capacity_moe.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**3D parallelism**

Data, tensor, and pipeline parallel scaling, ring all-reduce, and pipeline bubbles.

[Scaling to 1000 GPUs →](tutorials/06_scaling_1000_gpus.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Total cost of ownership**

Capital and operating cost, electricity, and per-query economics over any horizon.

[The $9M Question →](tutorials/08_nine_million_dollar.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Sustainability**

Energy, carbon footprint, and water use across datacenter regions.

[Geography Matters →](tutorials/07_geography.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Reliability**

Fleet MTBF, failure probability, and the Young-Daly checkpoint interval.

[Sensitivity Analysis →](tutorials/09_sensitivity.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Agents**

KV-cache footprints and stranded memory for long-running agent sessions.

[The Agent Zoo →](zoo/agents.qmd)
:::

::: {.sim-card .sim-card-link}
**Physical AI**

Stopping distances, information age, actuator limits, and fieldbus budgets for robots.

[The Embodied Zoo →](zoo/embodied.qmd)
:::

## Validate the approximation

The outputs are analytical estimates, not measurements. Use them to narrow the design space, expose assumptions, and choose the next experiment.

- **Check feasibility first.** If memory, network, or data movement is infeasible analytically, benchmarking will not rescue the design.
- **Calibrate efficiency.** Compute-heavy solvers expose an `efficiency` parameter. The defaults are literature-informed starting points; replace them with measured MFU or sustained throughput when you have it.
- **Compare regimes.** The most robust conclusions are binding constraints, crossover points, and sensitivity rankings.
- **Escalate fidelity deliberately.** Pick the few configurations worth validating with profiling, traces, or production load tests.

See the [accuracy and validation guide](accuracy.qmd) for how the solvers compare with published measurements.

## Companion material

MLSys·im pairs with the [Machine Learning Systems](https://mlsysbook.ai) textbook. The [lecture slides for Volume I](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol1.html){target="_blank"} and [Volume II](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol2.html){target="_blank"} cover the concepts; the [MLSys·im tutorial slides](slides.qmd) walk from a single-node roofline to fleet-scale carbon analysis.
